unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 11 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.3 - THEME 4: FAMILY LIFE & HOME

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will think about and search for the dynamics of family life by focusing on reunions, collaborative activities, and the generation gap. They will begin with interviews held with family members from different generations to learn about traditions, values, and perspectives. As a result of interviews, students will design and implement a creative family activity that incorporates intergenerational interests. They will video record the activity and share it in the classroom. Finally, students will reflect on their experiences in a short essay or visual presentation by summarising their insights on bridging the generation gap, the significance of family reunions, and the value of collaborative activities. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as family reunions; collaborative and creative activities at home; dealing with generation gap in families'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in after prep year 11 of upper secondary school may know what family reunions; collaborative and creative activities at home; dealing with generation gap in families mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in after prep year 11 of upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''family life and home'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.,
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in after prep year 11 of upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as family reunions; collaborative and creative activities at home; dealing with generation gap in families'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about dealing with generation gaps in families in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Problem-Solving Discussion Students work in small groups, and the teacher gives each group a scenario such as a ''generation gap issue'' or a ''family reunion planning problem''. Groups discuss the problem, suggest solutions using target vocabulary such as ''compromise'', ''acknowledge'', and ''respect boundaries'', and prepare a short summary. They present their solutions to the class by using target grammar, e.g. ''Our group suggests that families should acknowledge each other’s expectations''. After the presentation, the teacher gives feedback on the use of target vocabulary, target grammar, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe challenges in education in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Picture Match & Report The teacher gives students pictures representing family reunions, creative activities, and generation gap scenarios, labelled with target vocabulary such as ''a reunion'', ''bonding'', ''assembling'', and ''bridge the gap''. Students match the words with the pictures and create sentences, e.g. ''We bond during family reunions''. Then, in pairs, they share a memorable family moment by using simple sentences such as ''We host a family reunion every summer''. Their peers listen and report it to the class by using sentences such as ''He says that…'' or ''She tells me that…'' to practice the target grammar. After all pairs have presented, the teacher gives feedback on the use of the language with target vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
